## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools
- **Date:** 2026-05-27  
  **Link:** [OpenAI — Building self-improving tax agents with Codex](https://openai.com/index/building-self-improving-tax-agents-with-codex)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI described how it worked with Thrive and Crete on a Codex-based tax agent to automate filings, improve accuracy, and accelerate tax workflows.  
  **Why it matters:** This is a concrete signal that Codex is being positioned beyond code assistance into regulated, domain-specific agent workflows.

- **Date:** 2026-05-26  
  **Link:** [Google — Gemini API Interactions API breaking changes](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions-breaking-changes-may-2026)  
  **Summary:** Google’s Gemini Interactions API changed its default schema from legacy outputs to `steps`, with legacy support scheduled for removal on 2026-06-08.  
  **Why it matters:** Near-term breaking-change risk for production apps using Gemini Interactions; developers need to update parsing, streaming handlers, and `response_format` handling or pin old behavior.

- **Date:** 2026-05-27  
  **Link:** [OpenAI Help — Codex rate card](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001106-codex-rate-card)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI’s Codex rate card lists token-based credit costs across GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, and GPT-5.4-Mini usage.  
  **Why it matters:** Cost planning for Codex deployments now needs model-tier selection, not just usage volume.

- **Date:** 2026-05-27  
  **Links:** [Google Cloud workload identity](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation/google-cloud), [Kubernetes workload identity](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation/kubernetes)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI documented workload identity federation for Google Cloud and Kubernetes, allowing cloud-issued OIDC tokens to be exchanged for short-lived OpenAI access tokens.  
  **Why it matters:** Reduces static API-key exposure for production AI systems.
